simple.meaning: אַכְזָב (ʼakzâb) is a Hebrew word meaning “falsehood ; by implication treachery.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַכְזָב (H391) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Jeremiah 15:18, with occurrences in Jeremiah, Micah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַכְזָב (H391) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַכְזָב (H391) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַכְזָב (ʼakzâb) / H391 is traced through Jeremiah 15:18, Micah 1:14 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H391. akzab אַכְזָב adjective deceptive, disappointing (elative; opposed to אֵיתָן q. v. below יתן ) — only absolute singular: — Micah 1:14 (with play on proper name אַכְזִיב ); of a deceptive, disappointing stream (compare Isa 58:11 ) Jer 15:18 (|| נֶאְמָ֑נוּ לֹא מַיִם ; on meaning compare Job 6:15 ff.)

occurrences.englishText: Therefore you will give a parting gift to Moresheth Gath.
